title: Word Break
statement: You get a string and a list of allowed words. Decide whether the whole string can be cut into pieces so that every piece is an allowed word. You may use any word as many times as you like. Return true or false.

idea.sentence: dp[i] says whether the first i letters can be split into words. It is true when some cut j has dp[j] true and the piece s[j..i) is an allowed word.

jargon.plain: The first i letters of the string. dp[i] answers the question for that prefix.
A position j between letters. Everything before j is a smaller prefix we already solved; the rest is the last word.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the string, then the word list, e.g. "leetcode", ["leet","code"]

vars.meaning: length of the longest allowed word

compare.bruteLabel: Try every way to cut the string
compare.optimalLabel: One cell per prefix, one check per cut
compare.unit: cuts tried (rough; brute is exponential, 2n is the closest curve)

rows.name: Brute force recursion
rows.note: Tries every first word, then repeats for the rest. The same suffix is solved again and again.

rows.name: dp table
rows.note: n cells, up to n cuts each, and each slice and lookup costs about L. Skipping cuts longer than the longest word brings it to O(n · L²).

fast.takeaway: Whether a prefix splits only needs the answers for shorter prefixes, so the same sub-question is never solved twice.

stages.title: Base cell
stages.note: dp has n + 1 cells. dp[0] = true because the empty prefix splits into zero words.

stages.title: Find a good cut
stages.note: For each prefix length i, look for a cut j with dp[j] true and s[j..i) in the word set. One is enough.

stages.title: Answer
stages.note: The whole string is the prefix of length n, so the answer is dp[n].

edges.title: No word fits
edges.why: No cut gives an allowed word, so dp[1] stays false.

edges.title: Exactly one word
edges.why: The cut at 0 has dp[0] true and the piece "a" is a word, so dp[1] is true.

edges.title: Greedy prefix fails
edges.why: Taking goals leaves pecial, which is stuck. The table finds goal + special because it tries every cut.

edges.title: Many a then b
edges.why: A plain recursion explodes here. The table fills each prefix once and fails fast.

gotchas.text: The table is n + 1 long. dp[0] = true is not a special case in the loop: it is what lets the first word of the string, with cut 0, count.
Put the words in a set first. Searching the word list for every piece makes each check cost the list size instead of about one lookup.
s.slice(j, i) copies the piece, so the set lookup works by value. Strings compare by content in JS, unlike arrays, so a Set of strings is safe.
s[j:i] on a string is a cheap view with no copy. A map[string]bool is fine as a set. A missing key gives false, which is exactly the answer wanted here.

recap.key: dp[i] is true if some cut j has dp[j] true and s[j..i) is a word. dp[0] is true.
recap.complexity: Time O(n² · L). Space O(n) plus the word set.
moves: Put the words in a set
For each i, try cuts j: dp[j] and s[j..i) in the set
